content: {"summary":"In February 2025 the DNS lookups for orders‑api, auth‑service and catalog‑api timed out because the in‑cluster CoreDNS pods were CPU‑starved, while VMs bypassed CoreDNS and resolved normally. Scaling CoreDNS from 2 to 4 replicas and committing the new replica count (plus adding an alert on CoreDNS latency) restored name resolution.","likely_cause":"CoreDNS pods were CPU‑starved due to too few replicas, causing cluster‑wide DNS lookup failures.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"CoreDNS pods were CPU‑starved, causing DNS lookups to time out across namespaces.","evidence_ids":["INC-0016#2"],"quote":"Starve those CoreDNS pods of CPU and every namespace loses name resolution together"},{"text":"The issue was resolved by scaling CoreDNS to four replicas and committing the change to the manifest.","evidence_ids":["INC-0016#1","INC-0016#2"],"quote":"scaled coredns to 4 replicas ... lookups clean everywhere"}],"next_checks":["Verify CoreDNS replica count remains at least four","Implement or enable autoscaling for CoreDNS based on CPU usage","Add monitoring and alerting for CoreDNS request p99 latency"]}
